_comment: Per-metric limits for scripts/perf/check. Each rule matches a job and a metric (glob: * is any run of characters, dots too); later matching rules win. This file is the only place for limits. factor: a value worse than factor x the baseline median is a regression (default 1.5). min_delta: and at least this much worse, in the metric's unit (small timings jitter by more than half). ceiling (lower is better) and floor (higher is better): absolute limits, checked even before the history has 3 runs.

rules._ceiling: Passing runs fail 0 prompts (the median is 0, so the factor never fires): more than 5 is a broken model or GPU (the out-of-memory runs failed 130 to 140). A few are tolerated: interpretation retries a failed prompt.

rules._min_delta: A page's time moves by up to 3 s between loads of one run (100k: 27.5 to 31.3 s for the newest page).

rules._ceiling: The count of loads whose page never drew. A passing run draws every page; one that cannot is the finding the job exists to catch.
The count of the page's feed calls the executor answered with an error (its SPARQL eval deadline refused them). Above 0 is a refused load, whatever the history.

rules._metric: The executor's CPU over the loads, the space's own watch over its messages included: the auto-processor's cost lands here.

rules._min_delta: One busy core is 100. After the loads the space's watch keeps 1 to 2 cores busy; after the seeding the executor idles at 3 to 5.

rules._metric: The suite's own work (signing 12M links into a file), not the executor's: a change here is the host or the suite.
The executor's import rate (links over seed.import_s).

rules._factor: Fixed by the suite (12 links a message): a change is a change in what is seeded, not in the executor.

rules._metric: WE's timings of a person's waits in the built app (we: apps/we-web/e2e/coasys-spaces, README "Timings"), all in ms. A wait that shows on a page moves by up to a second between runs.
In the real tier: Unmute to the first heard word, the recording and the speech model included.
A call of the staging model, which can wait minutes behind other jobs on its one llama-server slot.
The canvas's zoom, pan, drag and select: input to the next painted frame, tens of ms.
The slowest of 5 rounds: one late frame (a garbage collection) doubles it.
The canvas's load: the click on Canvas to its first node.
Stub tier: the click on Canvas to every record drawn.
Real tier: the click on Canvas to the first record the model found drawn.

rules._min_delta: The default for the times of one call, in ms: a median of 0.3 ms to 30 ms moves by a few ms between runs. Every metric has one series per agent count (params agents), so 10 and 100 agents never compare.
A p95 is one slow call out of 10 to 100 (a scheduler pause, a flush): it jitters by tens of ms.

rules._metric: The slowest of N concurrent calls: as noisy as a p95.

rules._min_delta: The wall time of all agents at once: 0.2 to 20 s over the counts, with a spread of a few hundred ms.

rules._metric: The wall time of every user's perspective and links: it grows with the agent count by design, so the series is per count.

rules._min_delta: Stopping and starting a process is disk and scheduler bound: a second of spread.

rules._ceiling: Events of another user's perspective that reached a user. The test fails on it too; a passing run has none, so the median is 0 and the factor never fires.

rules._min_delta: Percent of one core over 30 s with no request. An idle executor is under 1 per cent at 10 agents; background work per agent shows as a rise with the count.
The memory one agent adds, in MiB: a tenth of a core's worth of spread is a MiB or two.

rules._factor: The executor's own gauges of perspectives and SPARQL stores held open: fixed by what the test creates, so a change is a change in what the executor keeps open.

rules._metric: The value at the largest agent count over the value at the smallest (a ratio, no unit). It is judged against its own history like the others: a ratio past 1.5x the median and 1 more is a metric that scales worse than it did. The test's own flags (per call above 2, totals above 15) are in its printed table, and do not fail a run.
